name: BFS / DFS Graph Traversal
description: Breadth-First Search (BFS) explores neighbors level by level using a queue, ideal for finding the shortest path in unweighted graphs. Depth-First Search (DFS) explores as far as possible along a branch using a stack or recursion, ideal for connectivity, cycle detection and topological ordering.
how_to_identify: Any problem on graphs or grids about reachability, connected components, shortest path (unweighted), or exploring all nodes without repeats.
use_cases: Shortest path in an unweighted grid
template: BFS: enqueue start, mark visited, and while the queue is non-empty pop, process, and enqueue unvisited neighbors in order. DFS: mark visited and recurse (or use an explicit stack) on unvisited neighbors.
space_complexity: O(V) for visited set plus queue/stack
common_mistakes: Forgetting to mark nodes visited before enqueueing, causing duplicate processing or infinite loops.
Using BFS where the graph is weighted (needs Dijkstra).
